Every code-panel banner in the app uses// this now (the sys_id hard-code notice used to be a separate .panel-warning; folded in here since// every one of these turned out to be explanatory, not a real warning about something risky).//// One icon, one border per panel, regardless of how many standards apply (GlideRecord/Script// Include can have up to three/four at once) - each tip is a <p> in .info-stack, hairline-// separated instead of stacking whole separate .panel-info boxes with a repeated icon each. The// icon is a sibling of .info-stack (not nested in the first tip) so it reads as labeling the// whole panel; its margin-top matches .info-stack p's own top padding so it still lands on// exactly the first line of text, not the vertical center of the full stack..gsb-widget .panel-info { display: flex; gap: var(--sp-sm); align-items: flex-start; padding: 0 var(--sp-lg); font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.45; background: var(--ed-info-bg); color: var(--ed-info-text); border-top: 1px solid var(--ed-info-border); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ed-info-border); }.gsb-widget .panel-info .ico { flex: 0 0 auto; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 17.4px; margin-top: var(--sp-sm); }.gsb-widget .panel-info .ico svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; }.gsb-widget .info-stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex: 1; min-width: 0; }.gsb-widget .info-stack p { margin: 0; padding: var(--sp-sm) 0; }.gsb-widget .info-stack p + p { border-top: 1px solid var(--ed-info-rule); }.gsb-widget .lint-banner { flex: 0 0 auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1px; }.gsb-widget .lint-item { display: flex; gap: var(--sp-sm); align-items: flex-start; padding: var(--sp-sm) var(--sp-xl); font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.45; }.gsb-widget .lint-item .ico { flex: 0 0 auto; display: flex; align-items: center; height: 17.4px; }.gsb-widget .lint-item .ico svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; }.gsb-widget .lint-item.danger { background: var(--ed-danger-bg); color: var(--ed-danger-text); border-top: 1px solid var(--ed-danger-border); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ed-danger-border); }.gsb-widget .lint-item.warn { background: var(--ed-warn-bg); color: var(--ed-warn-text); border-top: 1px solid var(--ed-warn-border); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ed-warn-border); }.gsb-widget pre.code {
  margin: 0; flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto;
  padding: var(--sp-xl) var(--sp-xl);
  font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.65;
  color: var(--ed-text); tab-size: 2; white-space: pre;
}.gsb-widget .c-kw { color: var(--ed-kw); }.gsb-widget .c-str { color: var(--ed-str); }.gsb-widget .c-num { color: var(--ed-num); }.gsb-widget .c-com { color: var(--ed-com); font-style: italic; }.gsb-widget .c-fn { color: var(--ed-fn); }.gsb-widget .phase-note {
  margin: var(--sp-xl) var(--sp-xl) 0; padding: var(--sp-md) var(--sp-lg);
  background: #221c0f; border: 1px solid #4d3f1c; border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  color: #fde68a; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5;
}.gsb-widget .stub-card { padding: var(--sp-xxl); text-align: center; color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; }// No inline <code> styling here on purpose - every <code> in this app (hint text like// `try/catch`, the Settings page's `{{vm.pageOrigin}}`, ...) renders as plain browser-default// monospace text. An earlier pass here added a chip look (background/padding/border-radius, plus// a --inline-code-bg theme token and a .modal-head-specific override) - removed, not needed.
]]></css>
<demo_data/>
<description>Glide Studio (AngularJS rebuild) - visual builder for ServiceNow GlideRecord, GlideAjax, GlideAggregate, Script Include, and Encoded Query scripts.</description>
<has_preview>true</has_preview>
<id>x_glide_studio_ng_widget</id>
<internal>false</internal>
<link><![CDATA[]]></link>
<name>Glide Studio</name>
<option_schema/>
<public>false</public>
<roles/>
<script><![CDATA[(function() {
  /* Server logic lives in the injected Angular services (ConnectionService/SchemaLiveService) - this widget needs no server-side data of its own. */
})();]]></script>
<servicenow>false</servicenow>
<sys_class_name>sp_widget</sys_class_name>
<sys_id>b2c3d4e5f60000112233445566778802</sys_id>
<sys_name>Glide Studio</sys_name>
<sys_scope display_value="Glide Studio">b2c3d4e5f60000112233445566778801</sys_scope>
<sys_update_name>sp_widget_b2c3d4e5f60000112233445566778802</sys_update_name>
<template><![CDATA[<div class="gsb-widget">
<div class="app" ng-cloak ng-class="{'meta-view': vm.activeMode === 'Settings' || vm.activeMode === 'Standards'}">

  <header class="appbar">
    <div class="appbar-brand"><span class="appbar-logo" aria-hidden="true">G</span>Glide Studio</div>
    <gs-select class="appbar-select" aria-label="Script type" ng-model="vm.activeMode"
               gs-options="vm.modeOptions" placeholder="Mode"></gs-select>
  </header>

  <nav class="sidenav" aria-label="Script type">
    <div class="sidenav-brand">
      <div class="sidenav-logo">G</div>
      <div>
        <p class="sidenav-brand-name">Glide Studio</p>
        <p class="sidenav-brand-desc">Visual ServiceNow script generator</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="sidenav-modes" role="radiogroup">
      <button type="button" class="sidenav-btn" ng-repeat-start="m in vm.modes" role="radio"
              ng-class="{active: vm.activeMode === m.key, connected: m.key === 'Settings' && vm.connection.status === 'connected', connecting: m.key === 'Settings' && vm.connection.status === 'connecting', error: m.key === 'Settings' && vm.connection.status === 'error'}"
              aria-checked="{{vm.activeMode === m.key}}" tabindex="{{vm.activeMode === m.key ? 0 : -1}}"
              ng-click="vm.selectMode(m.key)">
        <span ng-bind-html="m.icon"></span>
        <span class="sidenav-label">{{m.name}}</span>
        <span class="sidenav-badge" ng-if="!m.ready">soon</span>
        <span class="sidenav-conn-dot" ng-if="m.key === 'Settings'"></span>
      </button>
      <div class="sidenav-spacer" ng-if="m.key === 'Standards'" role="presentation" aria-hidden="true" ng-repeat-end></div>
      <button type="button" class="sidenav-btn" ng-click="vm.toggleTheme()"
              aria-pressed="{{vm.theme === 'dark'}}" title="Toggle dark mode">
        <svg ng-if="vm.theme === 'dark'" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4"/><path d="M12 2v2M12 20v2M4.93 4.93l1.41 1.41M17.66 17.66l1.41 1.41M2 12h2M20 12h2M6.34 17.66l-1.41 1.41M19.07 4.93l-1.41 1.41"/></svg>
        <svg ng-if="vm.theme !== 'dark'" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 12.79A9 9 0 1 1 11.21 3 7 7 0 0 0 21 12.79z"/></svg>
        <span class="sidenav-label">{{vm.theme === 'dark' ? 'Light mode' : 'Dark mode'}}</span>
      </button>
    </div>
  </nav>

  <div class="builder" ng-class="{'builder-focus-lock': vm.activeMode === 'Standards' && vm.stdFocusId}">
    <div class="page-title" ng-class="{'page-title-sticky': vm.activeMode === 'Standards'}">
      <span ng-bind-html="vm.activeModeInfo().headerIcon"></span>
      <div>
        <div class="page-title-name">{{vm.activeModeInfo().name}}</div>
        <div class="page-title-sub">{{vm.activeModeInfo().sub}}</div>
      </div>
      <div class="page-title-actions" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Standards' && vm.stdFocusId">
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-accent btn-sm" ng-click="vm.backFromStandards()">
          ← Back to {{vm.modeName(vm.previousMode)}}
        </button>
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.exitStdFocus()">
          Stay & browse Standards →
        </button>
      </div>
      <!-- Fallback copy of the rail's own search box (see .std-rail above) - the rail hides below
           std-rail-bp, and with no in-page nav at that width search needs somewhere else to live so
           it never disappears entirely. Hidden via CSS (.std-search-wrap-header, app.scss) whenever
           the rail's own copy is visible, so exactly one is ever shown; both bind vm.stdQuery so
           they can't drift. Mutually exclusive with the focus-mode actions above (vm.stdFocusId can
           only be truthy when vm.stdQuery is empty - see vm.openStandard/vm.selectMode), so only one
           of the two ever renders. -->
      <div class="page-title-actions" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Standards' && !vm.stdFocusId">
        <div class="std-search-wrap std-search-wrap-header">
          <input type="text" class="std-search-input" ng-model="vm.stdQuery" placeholder="Search standards…" aria-label="Search standards">
          <button type="button" class="std-search-clear" ng-if="vm.stdQuery" ng-click="vm.clearStdSearch()" aria-label="Clear search" title="Clear search">✕</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Shared context: one table + one connection status, persistent across every table-driven
         mode - see main.controller.js's vm.onWorkingTableChange for why this replaced five
         independent table pickers that could silently drift out of sync with each other. A card
         like every other panel (same title/spacing treatment), not a bespoke bar - "Source" as in
         the record source the rest of the panels below build against. -->
    <div class="card" ng-if="vm.usesWorkingTable(vm.activeMode)">
      <div class="card-head">
        <h2>Source</h2>
        <button type="button" class="working-context-conn" ng-click="vm.selectMode('Settings')" title="Go to Settings">
          <span class="working-context-dot" ng-class="vm.connection.status"></span>
          {{vm.connLabel()}}
        </button>
      </div>
      <div class="card-body">
        <div class="working-context-row">
          <div class="working-context-field">
            <span class="working-context-label">Table</span>
            <gs-select ng-model="vm.workingTable" ng-change="vm.onWorkingTableChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.tables" gs-live-search="vm.searchTables(query)" gs-label-for="vm.tableLabel(name)"
                       placeholder="table name" no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Type to search tables…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Not-yet-ported modes: placeholder, not a dead end - explains what's coming. -->
    <div class="card" ng-if="!vm.activeModeInfo().ready">
      <div class="stub-card">
        Phase 2 - {{vm.activeModeInfo().name}} hasn't been ported to this rebuild yet.<br>
        GlideRecord and GlideAggregate modes are fully wired - switch back to see them.
      </div>
    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideRecord'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Operation</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <div ng-class="{grid2: vm.vis.getMethod}">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldOperation">Operation</label>
              <gs-select id="fldOperation" ng-model="vm.state.operation" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.operations" placeholder="operation"></gs-select>
            </div>
            <div ng-if="vm.vis.getMethod">
              <label class="field-label">Lookup by</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.state.getMethod" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.getMethodOptions" placeholder="lookup by"></gs-select>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div ng-if="vm.vis.multiAction" style="margin-top:var(--sp-md);">
            <label class="field-label">Then...</label>
            <gs-select ng-model="vm.state.multiAction" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.multiActionOptions" placeholder="then"></gs-select>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Function</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">{{vm.fnHint}}</p>
          <div class="grid3">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldFnName">Function name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldFnName" autocomplete="off" placeholder="getIncident"
                     ng-model="vm.state.fnName" ng-change="vm.onFnNameEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldFnParams">Parameters</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldFnParams" autocomplete="off" placeholder="comma-separated parameters"
                     ng-model="vm.state.fnParams" ng-change="vm.onFnParamsEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldVarName">Variable name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldVarName" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.state.varName" ng-change="vm.onVarNameEdit()">
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.vis.exampleQuery">
        <div class="card-head">
          <h2>Example inputs</h2>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" ng-if="vm.connection.status === 'connected'" ng-click="vm.previewRecords()">▶ Preview records</button>
        </div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">These inputs don't change the generated function - they only build the example call shown in the output panel. Type an <code>encodedQuery</code>, or build one from conditions (a built query takes precedence).</p>
          <label class="field-label" for="fldExampleQuery">Encoded query</label>
          <input type="text" id="fldExampleQuery" placeholder="active=true^priority=1" autocomplete="off"
                 ng-model="vm.state.exampleQuery" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
          <div style="margin-top:var(--sp-md);">
            <gs-condition-groups groups="vm.state.grArgGroups" gs-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                                  gs-fields="vm.fieldNames(vm.state.table)" gs-table="vm.state.table" gs-conn="vm.connection"></gs-condition-groups>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.vis.exampleCard">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Example inputs</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">These inputs don't change the generated function - they only build the example call shown in the output panel.</p>
          <div ng-if="vm.vis.exampleSysId" style="margin-bottom:var(--sp-md);">
            <label class="field-label" for="fldExampleSysId">Sys ID</label>
            <input type="text" id="fldExampleSysId" placeholder="a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="vm.state.exampleSysId" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
          </div>
          <div ng-if="vm.vis.exampleSets">
            <div class="row" style="margin-bottom:var(--sp-sm);">
              <label class="check" style="cursor:default; white-space:nowrap; flex-shrink:0;">Caller passes an</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.state.insertInputStyle" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.insertStyleOptions" placeholder="input shape" style="max-width:230px;"></gs-select>
            </div>
            <p class="hint">The function sets whatever the caller passes in. List the fields you expect (with a sample value) to build the example call shown in the output panel.</p>
            <div class="set-row" ng-repeat="fld in vm.state.sets">
              <gs-select ng-model="fld.field" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.state.table)"
                         gs-exclude="name === 'number' || name.indexOf('sys_') === 0" placeholder="field"
                         no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
              <input type="text" placeholder="value" autocomplete="off" ng-model="fld.value" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
              <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeSet($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
            </div>
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addSet()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.vis.order">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Order & limit</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <label class="field-label">Order by</label>
          <div>
            <div class="order-row" ng-repeat="o in vm.state.orderBys">
              <gs-select ng-model="o.field" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.state.table)" placeholder="field name"
                         no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
              <gs-select ng-model="o.dir" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.orderDirOptions" placeholder="direction"></gs-select>
              <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeOrder($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addOrder()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add order field</button>

          <div class="row" style="margin-top:13px;">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.useLimit" ng-change="vm.onUseLimitChange()"> setLimit</label>
            <input type="number" min="1" style="max-width:110px;" ng-model="vm.state.limit" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
          </div>
          <p class="hint" ng-if="vm.vis.chooseWindow" style="margin:8px 0 0;">setLimit and chooseWindow can't be used together — turning on one turns the other off automatically.</p>
          <div ng-if="vm.vis.chooseWindow">
            <div class="row" style="margin-top:8px;">
              <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.useChooseWindow" ng-change="vm.onUseChooseWindowChange()"> chooseWindow</label>
              <input type="text" placeholder="first param" style="max-width:100px;" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.state.chooseWindowFirst" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
              <input type="text" placeholder="last param" style="max-width:100px;" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.state.chooseWindowLast" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            </div>
            <p class="hint" ng-if="vm.state.useChooseWindow" style="margin:6px 0 0;">Pagination should come from the caller, not be baked in - these become extra function parameters.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Options</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <p class="hint">These apply only where relevant to the current operation - options that don't apply are hidden.</p>
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.secure" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            Enforce ACLs <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>GlideRecordSecure</code></span>
          </label>
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.errorHandling" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            Add error handling <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>try/catch</code> + <code>gs.error</code></span>
          </label>
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.setWorkflow" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            Skip business rules <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>setWorkflow(false)</code></span>
          </label>
          <label class="check" ng-if="vm.vis.autoSysFields">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.autoSysFields" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            Skip updates to system fields <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>autoSysFields(false)</code></span>
          </label>
          <label class="check" ng-if="vm.vis.withRefs">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.state.withRefs" ng-change="vm.onFieldChange()">
            Cascade reference field updates <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>insertWithReferences() / updateWithReferences()</code></span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideQuery'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Operation</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <div ng-class="{grid2: vm.gqVis.getMethod}">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldGqOperation">Operation</label>
              <gs-select id="fldGqOperation" ng-model="vm.gqState.operation" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.gqOperations" placeholder="operation"></gs-select>
            </div>
            <div ng-if="vm.gqVis.getMethod">
              <label class="field-label">Lookup by</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.gqState.getMethod" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.getMethodOptions" placeholder="lookup by"></gs-select>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Function</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">{{vm.gqFnHint}}</p>
          <div class="grid3">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldGqFnName">Function name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldGqFnName" autocomplete="off" placeholder="getIncident"
                     ng-model="vm.gqState.fnName" ng-change="vm.onGqFnNameEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldGqFnParams">Parameters</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldGqFnParams" autocomplete="off" placeholder="comma-separated parameters"
                     ng-model="vm.gqState.fnParams" ng-change="vm.onGqFnParamsEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldGqVarName">Variable name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldGqVarName" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.gqState.gqVar" ng-change="vm.onGqVarEdit()">
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.gqVis.selectFields">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Fields to select</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Only these fields come back on the result. Leave empty to return the whole record.</p>
          <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.gqState.selectFields.length">None added - the whole record is returned.</div>
          <div class="si-field-row" ng-repeat="f in vm.gqState.selectFields track by $index">
            <gs-select ng-model="vm.gqState.selectFields[$index]" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.gqState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                       no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
            <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeGqField($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addGqField()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.gqVis.exampleQuery">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Example inputs</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">These inputs don't change the generated function - they only build the example call shown in the output panel. Type an <code>encodedQuery</code>, or build one from conditions (a built query takes precedence).</p>
          <label class="field-label" for="fldGqExampleQuery">Encoded query</label>
          <input type="text" id="fldGqExampleQuery" placeholder="active=true^priority=1" autocomplete="off"
                 ng-model="vm.gqState.exampleQuery" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()">
          <div style="margin-top:var(--sp-md);">
            <gs-condition-groups groups="vm.gqState.gqArgGroups" gs-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                                  gs-fields="vm.fieldNames(vm.gqState.table)" gs-table="vm.gqState.table" gs-conn="vm.connection"></gs-condition-groups>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.gqVis.exampleCard">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Example inputs</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">These inputs don't change the generated function - they only build the example call shown in the output panel.</p>
          <div ng-if="vm.gqVis.exampleSysId" style="margin-bottom:var(--sp-md);">
            <label class="field-label" for="fldGqExampleSysId">Sys ID</label>
            <input type="text" id="fldGqExampleSysId" placeholder="a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="vm.gqState.exampleSysId" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()">
          </div>
          <div ng-if="vm.gqVis.exampleSets">
            <p class="hint">GlideQuery applies whatever the caller passes directly - no per-field setValue loop to configure. List the fields you expect (with a sample value) to build the example call shown in the output panel.</p>
            <div class="set-row" ng-repeat="fld in vm.gqState.sets">
              <gs-select ng-model="fld.field" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.gqState.table)"
                         gs-exclude="name === 'number' || name.indexOf('sys_') === 0" placeholder="field"
                         no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
              <input type="text" placeholder="value" autocomplete="off" ng-model="fld.value" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()">
              <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeGqSet($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
            </div>
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addGqSet()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card" ng-if="vm.gqVis.order">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Order & limit</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <label class="field-label">Order by</label>
          <div>
            <div class="order-row" ng-repeat="o in vm.gqState.orderBys">
              <gs-select ng-model="o.field" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.gqState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                         no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
              <gs-select ng-model="o.dir" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()"
                         gs-options="vm.orderDirOptions" placeholder="direction"></gs-select>
              <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeGqOrder($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addGqOrder()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add order field</button>

          <div class="row" style="margin-top:13px;">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.gqState.useLimit" ng-change="vm.onGqUseLimitChange()"> limit</label>
            <input type="number" min="1" style="max-width:110px;" ng-model="vm.gqState.limit" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Options</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.errorHandling" ng-change="vm.onGqFieldChange()">
            Add error handling <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>try/catch</code> + <code>gs.error</code></span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideAggregate'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Aggregates</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Add one or more aggregate functions. A field is required for SUM / AVG / MIN / MAX; leave it empty for a plain COUNT, or set it for a distinct count.</p>
          <div class="agg-row" ng-repeat="a in vm.aggState.aggregates">
            <gs-select ng-model="a.fn" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.aggFnOptions" placeholder="function"></gs-select>
            <gs-select ng-model="a.field" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.aggState.table)"
                       gs-exclude="vm.isAggFieldExcluded(a.fn, vm.aggState.table, name)"
                       placeholder="field (optional for COUNT)"
                       no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
            <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeAggregate($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addAggregate()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add aggregate</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Function</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Parameters replace hardcoded values - the caller passes an <code>encodedQuery</code> string at runtime.</p>
          <div class="grid3">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAggFnName">Function name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAggFnName" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.aggState.fnName" ng-change="vm.onAggFnNameEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAggFnParams">Parameters</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAggFnParams" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.aggState.fnParams" ng-change="vm.onAggFnParamsEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAggVar">Variable name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAggVar" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.aggState.aggVar" ng-change="vm.onAggVarEdit()">
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head">
          <h2>Example inputs</h2>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" ng-if="vm.connection.status === 'connected'" ng-click="vm.previewAggregate()">▶ Preview results</button>
        </div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">These inputs don't change the generated function - they only build the example call shown in the output panel. Type an <code>encodedQuery</code>, or build one from conditions (a built query takes precedence).</p>
          <label class="field-label" for="fldAggExampleQuery">Encoded query</label>
          <input type="text" id="fldAggExampleQuery" placeholder="active=true^priority=1" autocomplete="off"
                 ng-model="vm.aggState.gaExampleQuery" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()">
          <div style="margin-top:var(--sp-md);">
            <gs-condition-groups groups="vm.aggState.groups" gs-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                                  gs-fields="vm.fieldNames(vm.aggState.table)" gs-table="vm.aggState.table" gs-conn="vm.connection"></gs-condition-groups>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Group by</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.aggState.groupBys.length">None added.</div>
          <div class="group-row" ng-repeat="g in vm.aggState.groupBys">
            <gs-select ng-model="g.field" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.aggState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                       no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
            <gs-select ng-model="g.order" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.groupOrders" placeholder="ordering"></gs-select>
            <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeGroupBy($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addGroupBy()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add group field</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Having</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Filter grouped results by an aggregate value (e.g. groups with COUNT > 5).</p>
          <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.aggState.havings.length">None added.</div>
          <div class="having-row" ng-repeat="h in vm.aggState.havings">
            <gs-select ng-model="h.fn" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.aggFnOptions" placeholder="function"></gs-select>
            <gs-select ng-model="h.op" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()"
                       gs-options="vm.havingOpOptions" placeholder="op"></gs-select>
            <input type="text" placeholder="value" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="h.value" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()">
            <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeHaving($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addHaving()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add having clause</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Options</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <p class="hint">Adding or removing a Group by field changes what this function returns — a single value with one aggregate and no grouping, an object keyed by aggregate with multiple aggregates, or an array of rows once any Group by field is added. If other code already calls this function, a change here can break it.</p>
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.errorHandling" ng-change="vm.onAggFieldChange()">
            Add error handling <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>try/catch</code> + <code>gs.error</code></span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideAjax'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Call setup</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Calls a client-callable Script Include (AbstractAjaxProcessor) from a client script. The method name maps to <code>sysparm_name</code>.</p>
          <div class="grid2">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAjaxSI">Script Include name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAjaxSI" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.ajaxState.ajaxScriptInclude" ng-change="vm.onAjaxSIEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAjaxMethod">Method (sysparm_name)</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAjaxMethod" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.ajaxState.ajaxMethod" ng-change="vm.onAjaxMethodEdit()">
            </div>
          </div>
          <label class="field-label" style="margin-top:13px;">Parameters</label>
          <p class="hint" style="margin-bottom:8px;">Names are auto-prefixed with <code>sysparm_</code>. Put quotes around literal text (e.g. <code>'active'</code>) to send it as-is; leave a value unquoted (e.g. <code>sysId</code>) to reference a variable defined earlier in your script.</p>
          <div class="param-row" ng-repeat="p in vm.ajaxState.ajaxParams">
            <input type="text" placeholder="name (sysparm_…)" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="p.name" ng-change="vm.onAjaxFieldChange()">
            <input type="text" placeholder="value or variable" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="p.value" ng-change="vm.onAjaxFieldChange()">
            <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeAjaxParam($index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
          </div>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addAjaxParam()" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add parameter</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Function</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint" style="margin-bottom:var(--sp-md);">GlideAjax is asynchronous - the caller passes a <code>callback</code> that receives the parsed answer instead of getting a return value.</p>
          <div class="grid3">
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAjaxFnName">Function name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAjaxFnName" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.ajaxState.fnName" ng-change="vm.onAjaxFnNameEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAjaxFnParams">Parameters</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAjaxFnParams" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.ajaxState.fnParams" ng-change="vm.onAjaxFnParamsEdit()">
            </div>
            <div>
              <label class="field-label" for="fldAjaxVar">Variable name</label>
              <input type="text" id="fldAjaxVar" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.ajaxState.ajaxVar" ng-change="vm.onAjaxVarEdit()">
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Options</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.errorHandling" ng-change="vm.onAjaxFieldChange()">
            Add error handling <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>try/catch</code> + <code>console.error</code></span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'ScriptInclude'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Source</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <label class="field-label" for="fldSiClassName">Script Include name</label>
          <input type="text" id="fldSiClassName" autocomplete="off"
                 ng-model="vm.siState.className" ng-change="vm.onSiClassNameEdit()">
          <div style="margin-top:var(--sp-md);">
            <label class="field-label" for="fldSiVarName">Variable name</label>
            <input type="text" id="fldSiVarName" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="vm.siState.varName" ng-change="vm.onSiVarNameEdit()">
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Client access</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.clientCallable" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
            Client-callable <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);">generates an <code>AbstractAjaxProcessor</code>, callable from a client script via <code>GlideAjax</code></span>
          </label>
          <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.clientCallable">
            <label class="check">
              <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.alsoServerClass" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
              Also build a server-side class <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);">the Ajax class delegates to it, instead of doing its own GlideRecord work</span>
            </label>
          </div>
          <p class="hint" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);" ng-if="vm.siState.clientCallable && !vm.siState.alsoServerClass">See the Example call panel for ready-to-paste <code>GlideAjax</code> usage.</p>
          <p class="hint" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);" ng-if="vm.siState.clientCallable && vm.siState.alsoServerClass">Generates the server class above plus a thin <code>AbstractAjaxProcessor</code> wrapper that delegates to it - keep server-only logic in the server class, and expose only what the client actually needs.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Methods</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <div class="method-block">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.create.on" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"> Create</label>
            <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.methods.create.on">
              <label class="check">
                <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.create.setWorkflow" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
                Skip business rules <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>setWorkflow(false)</code></span>
              </label>
              <label class="check">
                <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.create.autoSysFields" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
                Skip updates to system fields <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>autoSysFields(false)</code></span>
              </label>
              <label class="field-label" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">Return</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.create.returnType" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.siWriteReturnTypeOptions" placeholder="return type"></gs-select>
              <div ng-if="vm.siState.methods.create.returnType === 'object'" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">
                <label class="field-label">Return specific fields only <span class="hint">(leave empty for every field)</span></label>
                <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.siState.methods.create.fields.length">None added.</div>
                <div class="si-field-row" ng-repeat="f in vm.siState.methods.create.fields track by $index">
                  <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.create.fields[$index]" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"
                             gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.siState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                             no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
                  <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeSiField('create', $index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
                </div>
                <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addSiField('create')" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="method-block">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.read.on" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"> Get</label>
            <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.methods.read.on">
              <label class="field-label">Return</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.read.returnType" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.siReturnTypeOptions" placeholder="return type"></gs-select>
              <div ng-if="vm.siState.methods.read.returnType === 'object'" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">
                <label class="field-label">Return specific fields only <span class="hint">(leave empty for every field)</span></label>
                <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.siState.methods.read.fields.length">None added.</div>
                <div class="si-field-row" ng-repeat="f in vm.siState.methods.read.fields track by $index">
                  <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.read.fields[$index]" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"
                             gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.siState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                             no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
                  <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeSiField('read', $index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
                </div>
                <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addSiField('read')" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="method-block">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.list.on" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"> Query</label>
            <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.methods.list.on">
              <label class="field-label">Return</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.list.returnType" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.siListReturnTypeOptions" placeholder="return type"></gs-select>
              <div ng-if="vm.siState.methods.list.returnType === 'object'" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">
                <label class="field-label">Return specific fields only <span class="hint">(leave empty for every field)</span></label>
                <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.siState.methods.list.fields.length">None added.</div>
                <div class="si-field-row" ng-repeat="f in vm.siState.methods.list.fields track by $index">
                  <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.list.fields[$index]" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"
                             gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.siState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                             no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
                  <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeSiField('list', $index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
                </div>
                <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addSiField('list')" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
              </div>
              <label class="field-label" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">Limit <span class="hint">(optional - leave blank for no limit)</span></label>
              <input type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="e.g. 100" autocomplete="off"
                     ng-model="vm.siState.methods.list.limit" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="method-block">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.update.on" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"> Update</label>
            <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.methods.update.on">
              <label class="check">
                <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.update.setWorkflow" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
                Skip business rules <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>setWorkflow(false)</code></span>
              </label>
              <label class="check">
                <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.update.autoSysFields" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
                Skip updates to system fields <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>autoSysFields(false)</code></span>
              </label>
              <label class="field-label" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">Return</label>
              <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.update.returnType" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()" gs-options="vm.siWriteReturnTypeOptions" placeholder="return type"></gs-select>
              <div ng-if="vm.siState.methods.update.returnType === 'object'" style="margin-top:var(--sp-sm);">
                <label class="field-label">Return specific fields only <span class="hint">(leave empty for every field)</span></label>
                <div class="empty" ng-if="!vm.siState.methods.update.fields.length">None added.</div>
                <div class="si-field-row" ng-repeat="f in vm.siState.methods.update.fields track by $index">
                  <gs-select ng-model="vm.siState.methods.update.fields[$index]" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"
                             gs-options="vm.fieldNames(vm.siState.table)" placeholder="field name"
                             no-options-text="{{vm.connection.status === 'connected' ? 'Loading fields…' : 'No options'}}"></gs-select>
                  <button type="button" class="icon-btn" ng-click="vm.removeSiField('update', $index)" title="Remove">✕</button>
                </div>
                <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.addSiField('update')" style="margin-top:8px;">+ Add field</button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="method-block">
            <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.delete.on" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()"> Delete</label>
            <div class="method-sub" ng-if="vm.siState.methods.delete.on">
              <label class="check">
                <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.methods.delete.setWorkflow" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
                Skip business rules <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>setWorkflow(false)</code></span>
              </label>
            </div>
          </div>

        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Options</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body checks">
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.errorHandling" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
            Add error handling <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>try/catch</code> + <code>gs.error(this.type…)</code></span>
          </label>
          <label class="check">
            <input type="checkbox" ng-model="vm.siState.jsdoc" ng-change="vm.onSiFieldChange()">
            Add JSDoc comments <span class="hint" style="margin-left:var(--sp-sm);"><code>/** @param / @return */</code></span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Encoder'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Conditions</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Conditions inside a group are joined with <b>OR</b> (<code>^OR</code>); separate groups are joined with <b>AND</b> (<code>^</code>).</p>
          <gs-condition-groups groups="vm.encGroups" gs-change="vm.onEncFieldChange()"
                                gs-fields="vm.fieldNames(vm.encTable)" gs-table="vm.encTable" gs-conn="vm.connection"></gs-condition-groups>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <!-- The hosted GlideFast standards document (see StandardsService, generated from
         standards/glidefast-scripting-standards.md). Full-width like Settings (meta-view) -
         reference reading, no generated output. The std-link tips across the builder modes
         deep-link into these sections via vm.openStandard(id). Two columns on wide screens: a
         sticky rail on the left is the ONE nav for the doc (see main.controller.js's
         IntersectionObserver setup for vm.activeStdId, which keeps it synced to scroll position),
         and the reading column stays capped at .std-content's measure (860px) rather than
         stretching to fill the builder pane. The rail hides below std-rail-bp; with no in-page nav
         at that width, the reader falls back to plain scrolling (the sidenav itself already
         collapses to a mobile appbar well before that, so this is a narrow window-width band, not
         the actual mobile case). -->
    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Standards'" class="standards-doc" ng-click="vm.onStandardsClick($event)">

      <aside class="std-rail" ng-class="{'std-rail-locked': vm.stdFocusId}" aria-label="On this page">
        <!-- Search lives here (not just the header) so it sits with the rail, like the approved
             mockup - but the rail itself hides below std-rail-bp (see its own media query at the
             bottom of this block), so this copy would disappear at exactly the width where search
             is needed most. The header keeps its OWN copy (.std-search-wrap-header, index.html
             below) as a fallback, shown only when this one is hidden (see app.scss) - both bind the
             same vm.stdQuery, so they can never drift out of sync. -->
        <div class="std-search-wrap">
          <input type="text" class="std-search-input" ng-model="vm.stdQuery" placeholder="Search standards…" aria-label="Search standards">
          <button type="button" class="std-search-clear" ng-if="vm.stdQuery" ng-click="vm.clearStdSearch()" aria-label="Clear search" title="Clear search">✕</button>
        </div>
        <button type="button" class="std-rail-overview" ng-class="{active: vm.stdView === 'overview'}" ng-click="vm.showStdOverview()">Overview</button>
        <!-- Chapters, each expandable to its own sections - the rail stays to "principles and
             high-level topics" at rest (the mockup's own framing), with sections a click away
             rather than always-on clutter. Expand/collapse (vm.stdPartExpanded) is driven ONLY by
             the chevron button below (vm.toggleStdExpand) - clicking the chapter's own name just
             navigates, same as always, and never touches expand state either way (see
             main.controller.js's own comment on vm.stdExpanded for why). vm.stdPartHeadingActive
             lights the chapter's name up only when the reader is at its own heading, not a nested
             section (that gets its own highlight below, regardless of the chapter's expand state). -->
        <div class="std-rail-band" ng-repeat="grp in vm.standardsDoc.groups" ng-show="vm.stdGroupVisible(grp)">
          <button type="button" class="std-rail-band-title" ng-click="vm.openStandard(grp.id)">{{grp.name}}</button>
          <div class="std-rail-chapter" ng-repeat="part in grp.parts" ng-show="vm.stdPartVisible(part)">
            <div class="std-rail-part-row">
              <button type="button" class="std-rail-part"
                      ng-class="{active: vm.stdPartHeadingActive(part), 'std-dimmed': vm.stdFocusId && !vm.stdPartHasFocus(part)}"
                      ng-click="vm.openStandard(part.id)">{{part.title}}</button>
              <button type="button" class="std-rail-expand" ng-class="{expanded: vm.stdPartExpanded(part)}"
                      ng-click="vm.toggleStdExpand(part, $event)"
                      aria-label="{{vm.stdPartExpanded(part) ? 'Collapse' : 'Expand'}} {{part.title}} sections"
                      aria-expanded="{{vm.stdPartExpanded(part)}}">
                <svg width="10" height="10" viewBox="0 0 10 10" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M3 2l4 3-4 3"/></svg>
              </button>
            </div>
            <div class="std-rail-sections" ng-if="vm.stdPartExpanded(part)">
              <button type="button" class="std-rail-section" ng-repeat="section in part.sections" ng-show="vm.stdSectionMatches(section)"
                      ng-class="{active: vm.activeStdId === section.id, 'std-dimmed': vm.stdFocusId && vm.stdFocusId !== section.id}"
                      ng-click="vm.openStandard(section.id)">{{section.title}}</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </aside>

      <div class="std-doc-main">

        <!-- Overview is a real landing view, not just a scroll position: while active, the whole doc
             below (every .std-band) is kept OUT of the visible page via .std-reading-hidden
             (position:absolute + visibility:hidden - see app.scss), never display:none/ng-if. Two
             reasons: (1) the scroll-spy's IntersectionObserver already snapshotted every
             <h2 id="std-..."> when Standards mode was entered (see main.controller.js's activeMode
             $watch) - display:none would still leave those nodes findable, but visibility:hidden
             keeps them (2) GENUINELY LAID OUT the whole time, which real getBoundingClientRect()
             measurements depend on - display:none was tried first and caused a real, reproduced bug:
             the FIRST time ~20000px of never-yet-shown content went display:none -> block, Chrome's
             layout for that much fresh syntax-highlighted HTML took over a second, and
             StandardsUiService.scrollTo (which measures immediately) would compute a wildly short
             target, landing 5+ chapters early. Keeping it always laid out (just visually/
             positionally out of the way) means scrollTo's measurement is correct instantly, every
             time, with no retry/wait logic needed on its side. Picking a tile (or any rail link, or
             an external deep-link - all three route through vm.openStandard) flips vm.stdView to
             'reading', which drops the class and lets the content rejoin normal flow at its
             already-known height. A search query keeps the doc out of .std-reading-hidden regardless
             of vm.stdView, same as it already forced individual sections visible via ng-show. -->
        <div class="card" ng-show="vm.stdView === 'overview' || vm.stdQuery">
          <div class="card-head"><h2>Contents</h2></div>
          <div class="card-body">
            <!-- The hub: lead text + every chapter as a clickable tile, grouped by band. Ghost
                 "Planned" tiles (vm.standardsDoc.groups[].planned - see StandardsUiService) show
                 chapters that don't exist yet, so a thin band reads as a visible roadmap instead of
                 just sparse. -->
            <div ng-if="vm.stdView === 'overview' && !vm.stdQuery">
              <div class="std-content" ng-bind-html="vm.standardsDoc.lead"></div>
              <div class="std-hub">
                <div class="std-hub-band" ng-repeat="grp in vm.standardsDoc.groups">
                  <h3 class="std-hub-band-title">{{grp.name}}</h3>
                  <div class="std-hub-grid">
                    <button type="button" class="std-hub-tile" ng-class="{'std-hub-tile-alt': grp.name !== 'Principles'}" ng-repeat="part in grp.parts" ng-click="vm.openStandard(part.id)">
                      <span class="ic">
                        <svg ng-if="grp.name === 'Principles'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="9" cy="9" r="7"/><path d="M6 9.2l2 2 4-4.4"/></svg>
                        <svg ng-if="grp.name !== 'Principles'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 2L2 6.5l7 4.5 7-4.5L9 2z"/><path d="M2.5 9.5L9 13.5l6.5-4"/></svg>
                      </span>
                      <span class="t">{{part.title}}</span>
                      <span class="meta">{{part.sections.length}} section<span ng-if="part.sections.length !== 1">s</span></span>
                    </button>
                    <div class="std-hub-tile ghost" ng-class="{'std-hub-tile-alt': grp.name !== 'Principles'}" ng-repeat="p in grp.planned">
                      <span class="ic">
                        <svg ng-if="grp.name === 'Principles'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="9" cy="9" r="7"/><path d="M6 9.2l2 2 4-4.4"/></svg>
                        <svg ng-if="grp.name !== 'Principles'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 2L2 6.5l7 4.5 7-4.5L9 2z"/><path d="M2.5 9.5L9 13.5l6.5-4"/></svg>
                      </span>
                      <span class="t">{{p}}</span>
                      <span class="badge">Planned</span>
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div ng-if="vm.stdQuery">
              <p class="empty" ng-if="!vm.stdHasMatches()">No matching sections for "{{vm.stdQuery}}".</p>
              <p class="hint" ng-if="vm.stdHasMatches()">Showing sections matching "{{vm.stdQuery}}". <button type="button" class="std-link" ng-click="vm.clearStdSearch()">Clear search</button></p>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="std-band" ng-repeat="grp in vm.standardsDoc.groups" ng-show="vm.stdGroupVisible(grp)"
             ng-class="{'std-reading-hidden': vm.stdView !== 'reading' && !vm.stdQuery}">
          <h2 class="std-band-heading" id="std-{{grp.id}}">{{grp.name}}</h2>
          <div class="card" ng-repeat="part in grp.parts" ng-show="vm.stdPartVisible(part)">
            <div class="card-head" ng-class="{'std-dimmed': vm.stdFocusId && !vm.stdPartHasFocus(part)}"><h2 id="std-{{part.id}}">{{part.title}}</h2></div>
            <div class="card-body std-content">
              <div ng-class="{'std-dimmed': vm.stdFocusId}" ng-bind-html="part.lead"></div>
              <div ng-repeat="section in part.sections" ng-show="vm.stdSectionMatches(section)"
                   ng-class="{'std-dimmed': vm.stdFocusId && section.id !== vm.stdFocusId}"
                   ng-bind-html="section.html"></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

      </div>

    </div>

    <div ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Settings'">

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Connection</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint" ng-if="!vm.instanceHosted">Connect to a live ServiceNow instance to pull real table/field schema. Your instance admin must first add a <b>CORS Rule</b> (System Web Services > REST > CORS Rule) allowing this page's origin (<code>{{vm.pageOrigin}}</code>) for the Table API, with the <code>Authorization</code> header allowed. Username and password are remembered in this browser.</p>
          <p class="hint" ng-if="vm.instanceHosted">Running inside this ServiceNow instance - schema is pulled live using its own session automatically. No separate connection is needed.</p>

          <div ng-if="!vm.instanceHosted">
            <label class="field-label" for="fldConnUrl">Instance URL</label>
            <input type="text" id="fldConnUrl" placeholder="https://devXXXXX.service-now.com" autocomplete="off"
                   ng-model="vm.connection.instanceUrl" ng-change="vm.onConnUrlEdit()">
            <div class="grid2" style="margin-top:9px;">
              <div>
                <label class="field-label" for="fldConnUser">Username</label>
                <input type="text" id="fldConnUser" autocomplete="off" ng-model="vm.connection.username">
              </div>
              <div>
                <label class="field-label" for="fldConnPass">Password</label>
                <input type="text" id="fldConnPass" class="masked-input" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false"
                       data-1p-ignore data-lpignore="true" ng-model="vm.connection.password">
              </div>
            </div>
            <div class="row" style="margin-top:12px;">
              <button type="button" class="btn btn-accent btn-sm" ng-click="vm.connect()" ng-if="vm.connection.status !== 'connected'">Connect</button>
              <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger-ghost btn-sm" ng-click="vm.disconnect()" ng-if="vm.connection.status === 'connected'">Disconnect</button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <p class="hint" style="margin-top:9px;">{{vm.connStatusText()}}</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-head"><h2>Reset form</h2></div>
        <div class="card-body">
          <p class="hint">Reloads the page, returning everything to defaults. Your saved connection is kept.</p>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger-ghost" ng-click="vm.resetForm()">↺ Reset form</button>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- ng-show, not ng-if: this pane used to be destroyed/recreated on every Standards entry/exit,
       and even with gs-sync-attr setting data-editor-theme synchronously (so the attribute is never
       actually missing on a live digest), a freshly-inserted subtree's CSS custom properties could
       still show a one-frame flash of the wrong (light) colors in dark mode - a browser rendering
       quirk on brand new nodes, not an Angular timing gap. ng-show never destroys the element; it
       just toggles display:none (zero layout cost, same as ng-if, since it's THE global .ng-hide
       rule), so there's no fresh insertion event at all when leaving Standards. (The SEPARATE
       raw-HTML-paints-before-Angular-bootstraps gap that gs-sync-attr alone doesn't cover is handled
       once, at the root - see the ng-cloak comment on .app above - not per-element here.) -->
  <div class="output-pane" ng-show="vm.activeMode !== 'Settings' && vm.activeMode !== 'Standards'" gs-sync-attr="'data-editor-theme'" gs-sync-value="vm.editorThemeApplied">
    <div class="out-top">
      <span class="title">{{vm.outputTitle()}}</span>
      <button type="button" class="editor-theme-toggle" ng-click="vm.cycleEditorTheme()"
              title="{{'Code editor theme: ' + vm.editorThemeLabel() + ' (independent of the app theme) — click to change'}}"
              aria-label="{{'Code editor theme: ' + vm.editorThemeLabel() + ' — click to change'}}">
        <svg ng-if="vm.editorTheme === 'light'" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4"/><path d="M12 2v2M12 20v2M4.93 4.93l1.41 1.41M17.66 17.66l1.41 1.41M2 12h2M20 12h2M6.34 17.66l-1.41 1.41M19.07 4.93l-1.41 1.41"/></svg>
        <svg ng-if="vm.editorTheme === 'dark'" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 12.79A9 9 0 1 1 11.21 3 7 7 0 0 0 21 12.79z"/></svg>
        <svg ng-if="vm.editorTheme === 'auto'" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 3a9 9 0 000 18z" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
      </button>
    </div>
    <div class="lint-banner" role="alert" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideRecord' && vm.lintWarningsList.length">
      <div class="lint-item" ng-class="w.level" ng-repeat="w in vm.lintWarningsList">
        <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10.29 3.86L1.82 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.71 3h16.94a2 2 0 0 0 1.71-3L13.71 3.86a2 2 0 0 0-3.42 0z"/><line x1="12" y1="9" x2="12" y2="13"/><line x1="12" y1="17" x2="12.01" y2="17"/></svg></span>
        <span>{{w.msg}} <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-if="w.stdId" ng-click="vm.openStandard(w.stdId)">Standard: {{w.stdTitle}} ▸</button></span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lint-banner" role="alert" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideQuery' && vm.gqLintWarningsList.length">
      <div class="lint-item" ng-class="w.level" ng-repeat="w in vm.gqLintWarningsList">
        <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10.29 3.86L1.82 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.71 3h16.94a2 2 0 0 0 1.71-3L13.71 3.86a2 2 0 0 0-3.42 0z"/><line x1="12" y1="9" x2="12" y2="13"/><line x1="12" y1="17" x2="12.01" y2="17"/></svg></span>
        <span>{{w.msg}} <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-if="w.stdId" ng-click="vm.openStandard(w.stdId)">Standard: {{w.stdTitle}} ▸</button></span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="panels">
      <div class="panel">
        <div class="panel-bar">
          <span class="panel-title">{{vm.mainPanelTitle()}}</span>
          <div class="panel-actions">
            <button type="button" class="panel-icon-btn" ng-class="{copied: vm.copyStatus !== 'Copy'}"
                    data-tip="Copy" aria-label="Copy" ng-click="vm.copyCode()">
              <svg ng-if="vm.copyStatus === 'Copy'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="9" y="9" width="13" height="13" rx="2"/><path d="M5 15H4a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h9a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v1"/></svg>
              <svg ng-if="vm.copyStatus !== 'Copy'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><polyline points="20 6 9 17 4 12"/></svg>
            </button>
            <button type="button" class="panel-icon-btn" data-tip="Download" aria-label="Download" ng-click="vm.downloadCode()">
              <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 15v4a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2v-4"/><polyline points="7 10 12 15 17 10"/><line x1="12" y1="15" x2="12" y2="3"/></svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideRecord'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>Wrapping the code in a named function keeps its variables out of the shared scope, where they could collide with other scripts. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('wrap-code-in-a-function')">Standard: Wrap code in a function ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.vis.getMethod">The generated get is guarded so a missing record never breaks the caller. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('verify-values-exist-before-using-them')">Standard: Verify values exist before using them ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.vis.order">Cap what a query returns - pulling every row on a large table doesn't scale. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('avoid-complex-queries-on-large-data-sets')">Standard: Avoid complex queries on large data sets ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.vis.exampleSets">Each field is set with setValue() - the explicit, type-safe counterpart to getValue() - never a direct property assignment. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('set-fields-with-setvalue-and-setdisplayvalue')">Standard: Set fields with setValue() ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.state.secure">GlideRecordSecure honors the caller's ACLs, so a query driven by a user's request can't return records they aren't allowed to see. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('enforce-acls-in-server-code-with-gliderecordsecure')">Standard: Enforce ACLs in server code ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.errorHandling">The generated try/catch logs the failure and fails safely instead of aborting the whole transaction. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('handle-errors-gracefully')">Standard: Handle errors gracefully ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideQuery'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>GlideQuery is null-safe and strict - a missing record has to be handled explicitly (<code>orElse</code>), and a mistyped field name throws instead of quietly returning an empty string. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('prefer-glidequery-for-clear-safe-queries')">Standard: Prefer GlideQuery for clear, safe queries ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.gqVis.getMethod">The generated get is guarded so a missing record never breaks the caller. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('verify-values-exist-before-using-them')">Standard: Verify values exist before using them ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.gqVis.order">Cap what a query returns - pulling every row on a large table doesn't scale. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('avoid-complex-queries-on-large-data-sets')">Standard: Avoid complex queries on large data sets ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.errorHandling">The generated try/catch logs the failure and fails safely instead of aborting the whole transaction. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('handle-errors-gracefully')">Standard: Handle errors gracefully ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideAggregate'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>GlideAggregate asks the database to count or sum, instead of retrieving every matching record first - it scales far better on large tables. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('use-glideaggregate-for-simple-record-counting')">Standard: Use GlideAggregate for record counting ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.errorHandling">The generated try/catch logs the failure and fails safely instead of aborting the whole transaction. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('handle-errors-gracefully')">Standard: Handle errors gracefully ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'GlideAjax'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>An async GlideAjax call is the preferred way to pull server data your client script doesn't already have - much lighter than a client-side GlideRecord lookup. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('minimize-server-lookups')">Standard: Minimize server lookups ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.errorHandling">The generated try/catch logs the failure and fails safely instead of letting the call error silently. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('handle-errors-gracefully')">Standard: Handle errors gracefully ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'ScriptInclude'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>Give the class and its GlideRecord a specific, descriptive name - never the generic <code>gr</code>. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('use-descriptive-names')">Standard: Use descriptive names ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.siState.clientCallable && !vm.siState.alsoServerClass">A Script Include only loads when it's actually called, unlike a global Business Rule or Client Script, which loads on every page. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('prefer-script-includes-to-global-scripts')">Standard: Prefer Script Includes to global scripts ▸</button></p>
            <p>Script Includes are the standard home for reusable server-side logic - small, specialized methods that other scripts call. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('create-small-modular-components')">Standard: Create small, modular components ▸</button></p>
            <p>Each method returns a value the caller can act on - a record, a success flag, or null on failure. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('return-a-meaningful-value')">Standard: Return a meaningful value ▸</button></p>
            <p ng-if="vm.errorHandling">The generated try/catch logs the failure and fails safely instead of aborting the whole transaction. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('handle-errors-gracefully')">Standard: Handle errors gracefully ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="panel-info" ng-if="vm.activeMode === 'Encoder'">
          <span class="ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12.01" y2="8"/></svg></span>
          <div class="info-stack">
            <p>Building the filter here and copying its encoded query string is easier to get right - and easier to update later - than chaining <code>addQuery()</code>/<code>addOrCondition()</code> calls by hand. <button type="button" class="std-link std-link-ed" ng-click="vm.openStandard('avoid-complex-gliderecord-queries')">Standard: Prefer encoded queries for complex filters ▸</button></p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <pre class="code" ng-bind-html="vm.currentHtml()"></pre>
      </div>
      <div class="panel" ng-if="vm.currentExampleCode()">
        <div class="panel-bar">
          <span class="panel-title">Example call</span>
          <div class="panel-actions">
            <button type="button" class="panel-icon-btn" ng-class="{copied: vm.exampleCopyStatus !== 'Copy'}"
                    data-tip="Copy" aria-label="Copy" ng-click="vm.copyExampleCode()">
              <svg ng-if="vm.exampleCopyStatus === 'Copy'" width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="9" y="9" width="13" height="13" rx="2"/><path d="M5 15H4a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h9a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v1"/></svg>
